items.stem: An ideal transformer has a 10:1 turns ratio (primary:secondary). If the primary voltage is 2400 V, the secondary voltage is:

options.rationale: Correct: secondary voltage equals primary divided by the turns ratio, 2400 / 10 = 240 V.
This multiplies rather than divides by the turns ratio.
A step-down transformer changes the voltage; it is not equal.
This uses a ratio of 2:1, not 10:1.

items.explanation: Correct: secondary voltage equals primary divided by the turns ratio, 2400 / 10 = 240 V.

items.stem: For overcurrent protection to be selective (coordinated), a downstream device should operate:

options.text: Faster than the upstream device for a fault beyond it
options.rationale: Correct: the device closest to the fault should clear first so only the faulted section is isolated.
If the downstream device is slower, the upstream device may trip first and remove more of the system.

options.text: At exactly the same time as every other device

options.rationale: Coordination concerns automatic timing, not manual reset.

items.explanation: Correct: the device closest to the fault should clear first so only the faulted section is isolated.

items.stem: In a balanced three-phase system, which TWO relationships hold for a wye (star) connection?

options.rationale: Correct: in a wye connection the line and phase currents are equal.

options.text: Line voltage is the square root of three times the phase voltage
options.rationale: Correct: wye line voltage is the square root of three times phase voltage.
That relationship holds for a delta connection, not wye.

options.text: Power is zero in a balanced system
options.rationale: A balanced system still delivers power.

options.text: Frequency depends on the load impedance
options.rationale: System frequency is set by the source, not the load impedance.

items.explanation: Correct: in a wye connection the line and phase currents are equal.
